'''Haïm Brezis''' (1 June 1944 – 7 July 2024) was a French mathematician, who mainly worked in [[functional analysis]] and [[partial differential equation]]s.

==Biography==
Born in [[Riom-ès-Montagnes]], [[Cantal]], France. Brezis was the son of a [[Romanians|Romanian]] immigrant father, who had come to France in the 1930s, and a Jewish mother who had fled from the Netherlands. His wife, [[Michal Govrin]], is an Israeli novelist, poet, and theater director.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.haaretz.com/oh-my-love-comely-as-jerusalem-1.47474 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104075716/http://www.haaretz.com/oh-my-love-comely-as-jerusalem-1.47474 |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 November 2012 |title=Oh my love, comely as Jerusalem |date=18 April 2002 |accessdate=21 October 2010 |newspaper=[[Haaretz|Haaretz Daily Newspaper]]|author=Dalia Karpel}}</ref> Brezis received his Ph.D. from the [[University of Paris]] in 1972 under the supervision of [[Gustave Choquet]]. He was a professor at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] and a visiting distinguished professor at [[Rutgers University]]. He was a member of the [[Academia Europaea]] (1988) and a foreign associate of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] (2003). In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 10 November 2012.</ref> He held honorary doctorates from several universities including [[National Technical University of Athens]].<ref>{{cite web|title=DHC National Technical University of Athens|url=http://www.semfe.ntua.gr/el/announcements/prosklisi-gia-tin-teleti-epitimopoiisis-tou-kath-h-brezis|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191103113436/http://www.semfe.ntua.gr/el/announcements/prosklisi-gia-tin-teleti-epitimopoiisis-tou-kath-h-brezis|archive-date=2019-11-03|url-status=dead }}</ref> Brezis is listed as an [[ISI highly cited researcher]].<ref>{{cite web|title=List of ISI highly cited researchers|url=http://highlycited.com}}</ref> He also served on the Mathematical Sciences jury for the [[Infosys Prize]] in 2013 and 2014. In 2024 he was awarded the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Lifetime Achievement of the AMS.

Brezis died in [[Jerusalem]] on 7 July 2024, at the age of 80.<ref>{{cite web|title=Décès de Haïm Brézis|url=https://smf.emath.fr/actualites-smf/deces-de-haim-brezis|publisher=[[Société Mathématique de France]]|accessdate=8 July 2024}}</ref>

==Works==
*''Opérateurs maximaux monotones et semi-groupes de contractions dans les espaces de Hilbert ''(1973)
*''Analyse Fonctionnelle. Théorie et Applications ''(1983)
* ''Haïm Brezis. Un mathématicien juif''. Entretien Avec Jacques Vauthier. Collection Scientifiques & Croyants. Editions Beauchesne, 1999. {{isbn|978-2-7010-1335-0}}, {{isbn|2-7010-1335-6}}
* ''Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations'', Springer; 1st Edition. edition (10 November 2010), {{isbn|978-0-387-70913-0}}, {{isbn|0-387-70913-4}}
